zero_omission_notes.summary: Details physical/chemical traits of metals and non-metals, ionic compound formation, reactivity series, extraction metallurgy (roasting, calcination, thermit process), and corrosion prevention.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Metals are malleable, ductile, lustrous, good conductors. Exceptions: Mercury is liquid; Gallium/Caesium melt on palm; Iodine is lustrous non-metal; Carbon graphite conducts electricity.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Ductility of Gold
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Gold is the most ductile metal; 1 gram of gold can be drawn into a wire 2 km long.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.activity_or_method_id: Activity 3.12: Action of Iron Nail on CuSO4 Solution
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: To demonstrate metal displacement based on reactivity series.
procedure_or_steps: Immerse iron nail in blue CuSO4 solution for 20 minutes.
Observe color change in solution and nail surface.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Blue CuSO4 solution turns pale green (FeSO4); reddish-brown copper deposits on iron nail.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Iron is more reactive than copper: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu.

short_answer_questions.question: Give reasons why Aluminium is used for cooking utensils despite high reactivity.
short_answer_questions.answer: Aluminium reacts with oxygen to form a thin, strong, non-porous protective oxide layer (Al2O3) that prevents further corrosion. It is also light and a good conductor of heat.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Describe the electrolytic refining of crude copper with diagram setup details.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: Anode: Impure crude copper block. Cathode: Thin sheet of pure copper. Electrolyte: Acidified CuSO4 solution. On passing current, pure Cu dissolves from anode and deposits at cathode (Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu). Insoluble impurities settle at bottom as anode mud.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Iron nails placed in test tube A (water+air) rust, but nails in B (boiled water+oil layer) and C (dry calcium chloride) do not.

qa.question: What conditions are essential for iron rusting based on this experiment?
qa.answer: Both oxygen (air) and moisture (water) are simultaneously required for rusting.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Thinking ionic compounds conduct electricity in solid state.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: State that ionic compounds conduct electricity only in molten or aqueous state due to free moving ions.
